content.value_statement: Production teams need clear reliability targets and repeatable incident practices. This skill provides SRE templates for SLOs, error budgets, alerting, and postmortems.
actual_capabilities: Explains how SLAs, SLOs, and SLIs relate to service reliability.
Provides availability and latency SLI formulas for Prometheus metrics.
Defines error budget actions for normal work, risky changes, and freezes.
Supplies standard and quick postmortem templates for incidents.
Provides multi-window burn rate alert examples and dashboard guidance.
Includes a verifier script for required skill files and sections.
limitations: It does not connect to monitoring systems or deploy alert rules automatically.
Prometheus examples require adaptation to each service metric schema.
It cannot determine business impact without user-provided incident context.
It does not replace organization-specific incident command procedures.

use_cases.title: Set Service Reliability Targets
use_cases.description: Define SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets for a production API or user-facing service.

use_cases.title: Create Incident Postmortems
use_cases.description: Turn incident notes into a clear blameless report with timeline, impact, root cause, and action items.

use_cases.title: Design Burn Rate Alerts
use_cases.description: Draft Prometheus alerting rules and dashboard guidance for availability and latency objectives.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Basic SLO
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one service objective.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define an availability SLO for this service. Include the SLI, target, measurement window, and simple error budget policy.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Postmortem
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the standard postmortem template for this incident. Organize the summary, UTC timeline, impact, 5 Whys analysis, and action items.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Error Budget Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SLO status and recommend actions for the remaining error budget. Include release policy, risk controls, and owner follow-ups.

prompt_templates.title: Build Burn Rate Alerting
prompt_templates.prompt: Design multi-window burn rate alerts for these Prometheus metrics. Include fast burn, slow burn, budget exhausted alerts, and dashboard panels.

output_examples.input: A team needs a 99.9 percent availability objective for an API.
output_examples.output: The response defines successful requests over total requests, a 28-day target, downtime budget, and actions when budget drops.

output_examples.input: An incident caused 40 minutes of degraded checkout service.
output_examples.output: The response produces a blameless postmortem outline with executive summary, UTC timeline, impact, root cause prompts, and assigned actions.

output_examples.input: A platform team wants burn rate alerts for latency and availability.
output_examples.output: The response recommends fast and slow burn windows, alert severities, dashboard panels, and common alerting mistakes to avoid.

best_practices: Provide service metrics, customer impact, and current alert behavior before asking for recommendations.
Adapt every SLO target to business needs instead of copying example percentages unchanged.
Assign owners, due dates, and tickets to postmortem action items.
anti_patterns: Do not target 100 percent availability unless the business can fund the operational cost.
Do not alert only on raw SLI values without error budget burn context.
Do not write postmortems that blame individuals instead of improving systems.

faq.question: What production problems does this skill address?
faq.answer: It helps define SLOs, manage error budgets, design alerts, and document incidents with blameless postmortems.

faq.question: Can it deploy Prometheus alert rules?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and structure, but users must adapt and deploy rules in their monitoring environment.

faq.question: Does it support incident response meetings?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a postmortem meeting structure, facilitation tips, and action item guidance.

faq.question: Is it useful for early application development?
faq.answer: It is intended for operating services in production, not for initial application scaffolding.

faq.question: What monitoring systems are referenced?
faq.answer: The examples focus on Prometheus recording rules, burn rate alerts, and Grafana-style dashboard concepts.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
